title: Cross-team slice coordination notebook (working)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working notebook for coordinating small-batch canaries, A/B oscillations, and slice-level quarantines across multiple teams. It focuses on human-gated handoffs, minimal-traffic experiments, and rapid escape hatches for model/route regressions. Not meant to replace the canonical runbook but to capture cross-team heuristics, mini-scripts, and simulation scenarios we keep revising.

Summary (one-paragraph):
Cross-team canaries succeed when the traffic partitioning, observability signals, and human role choreography are explicit and rehearsed. This doc bundles a compact coordination matrix, activation checklist, staged simulation scenarios, and short communication templates that SRE, Product, Safety, and Console Ops can use during low-latency LLM feature rollouts.

Quick glossary (short):
- slice: a traffic partition defined by product + cohort (e.g., search-power-users, mobile-new-installs)
- steward: the person accountable for obs/rollback during an activation window
- steward-adjacent: someone who can perform escalation steps (SRE oncall, Safety oncall)
- escape hatch: an automated or manual switch that forces traffic away from the experimental variant

Roles & responsibilities (compact):
- Product steward (owner): defines hypothesis, expected signals, and exposure cadence. Primary contact for product decisions.
- Observability steward (SRE): validates metrics, synthetic probes, tail latency, and error channels. Executes rollback commands if infra signals fail.
- Safety steward (Safety): monitors behavioral/eval signals, flags content regressions, and authorizes content-related rollbacks.
- Console Ops (Console): flips routing, monitors quotas, ensures traffic split applied correctly.
- Solutions/SE (optional): customer-facing comms for any impacted enterprise slices.

Activation checklist (pre-activation):
- Confirm hypothesis & minimal viable metrics (latency, CTR proxy, safety score).
- Define primary / secondary signals and quick numeric thresholds for immediate rollback. Document in Slack header and the Canary ticket.
- Create short-lived synthetic traffic job: 1000 requests over 15 minutes with representative prompts. Link synthetic job id to ticket.
- Reserve steward coverage window (primary + one backup) and add to calendar with pager contact.
- Prepare quick rollback commands (CLI snippet) and test in staging.
- Verify model variant routing configuration: verify route ids and percent targets.
- Set budget guard: max token spend / per-minute rate limits for the slice.

Activation checklist (during activation):
- Start with 0.5% of global traffic or a microcohort (e.g., internal employees) for 15–30m.
- Observe synthetic job and live telemetries: latency P95/P99, error rate, user-visible failure rate, safety regressions.
- Run the behavioral smoke test (5 representative prompts) from two geographic regions.
- If any primary signal breaches threshold, trigger escape hatch and notify stakeholders immediately.

Slice coordination matrix (example entries):
- search-batch (product): Product steward Maya H.; SRE Evan L.; Safety Priya N.; Console Ops Leah B.; initial share 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% over 3 waves.
- rerank-mobile (product): Product steward Carlos O.; SRE backup: Oncall SRE; Safety: Safety-oncall; start with 1% internal users.

Telemetry & signals (priority order):
1) Latency P95 and P99 (increase relative to baseline > 25% = alarm).
2) Token error rate / truncated outputs (>0.3% absolute increase).
3) Safety classifier delta by cohort (>2.5% relative increase).
4) Business proxy (CTR, completion acceptance) - directional but slower.
5) Infrastructure anomalies (GPU OOM, scheduler backpressure).

Suggested numeric thresholds (starter heuristics):
- Latency P99: +25% vs baseline OR absolute > 2.5s for chat routes.
- Error rate: +0.3 percentage points vs baseline (for low-base error signals).
- Safety delta: +2.5% relative increase in flagged outputs over 15m window.
- Cost spike: per-minute token spend > 2x expected for a slice.

Quarantine & rollback decision flow (text outline):
1) Detection: signal crosses threshold and observed in both synthetic and live traffic.
2) Triage: steward + steward-adjacent confirm signal, collect top N sample outputs and trace ids.
3) Short-circuit: flip escape hatch to route 95%+ traffic to baseline model/route.
4) Post-rollback: create a short incident note in the ticket (cause unknown / suspected cause).
5) Recovery plan: staged re-try window only after root cause actions or model retrain/patch.

Simulation scenarios (to rehearse before high-exposure rollouts):
- Scenario A - latency tail regression: inject latency in model runner for 10 minutes, confirm P99 alarm triggers and console Ops run rollback command within 5 minutes.
- Scenario B - safety spike: send 1000 crafted prompts that trigger safety classifier; ensure Safety steward receives samples and authorizes quarantine.
- Scenario C - oscillation under A/B: two model variants cause alternating user acceptance; observe for oscillation patterns and design a hold-back pattern to stabilize.

Short CLI snippets for rollback (example, adapt to prod CLI):
- show routes: redwood routes list --env prod --slice rerank-mobile
- set split: redwood routes set-split --route rerank-mobile --variant baseline --percent 100 --reason "emergency-rollback"
(keep these in the ticket so anyone with Console Ops access can copy/paste).

Communication templates (Slack / Pager):
- Immediate alert (Slack):
[ALERT] Canary rollback triggered for rerank-mobile (slice). Steward: Maya H. Reason: safety-delta +3.1%. Action: console routed -> baseline. Oncall SRE investigating. Ticket: ENG-4123.

- Post-rollback status update (Slack):
Status update: Canary for rerank-mobile rolled back at 14:07 UTC. Current traffic: baseline 100%. Primary signals: safety classifier spike confirmed; latency nominal. Samples uploaded to ticket. Next steps: Safety deep-dive + re-eval prompt filters.

Postmortem & learning capture (short template):
- What happened (timeline with events and timestamps).
- Immediate impact (user visible/metrics).
- Root cause (hypothesis and evidence).
- Action items (owners + due dates).
- Guardrail changes (new thresholds/test coverage).

Small experiments: slice composability heuristics to try next sprint
- staggered de-risk slices: allocate 3 sibling micro-slices instead of single 1% slice to spread sampling diversity.
- deliberate synthetic-probe skew: send edge-case prompts only to the canary to accelerate safety detection.
- token budget envelope: enforce per-slice hard cap with soft warnings at 60/80/95%.

Open questions / TODOs (scratchpad):
- Should we make the synthetic-probe runner a first-class resource in Console to auto-attach to every canary ticket?
- Standardize a single small payload/5 prompt smoke test per route so signal comparisons are faster.
- Run a cross-team dry-run exercise next month and capture time-to-rollback metrics.

Appendix: quick sample ticket stub (copy/paste):
Title: CANARY: rerank-mobile -> model-v10 (0.5% -> 2% step)
Assignee: Product steward Maya H.
Start window: 2025-02-15 16:00-17:30 UTC
Hypothesis: model-v10 improves CTR by >2% with no safety regressions
Primary signals: latency P99, safety-delta, error-rate
Synthetic job id: synth-20250215-01
Rollback commands: (see CLI snippets above)
Contact: @maya.h @evan.l @safety-oncall

Notes: This doc is a living notebook; use it as a rehearsal and then move the distilled checklists into the canonical runbook once validated. Please add simulation results and small empirical numbers after any rehearsal.

---
Last edits: 2025-02-08 by Maya Hernandez (draft); collaborators added notes on scenario C and suggested threshold tuning for chat routes.
